sections.heading: How do the synergy ratings work?

p: Each synergy has a letter. S is run-defining, A is strong, B is good, C is minor, and D marks items that work against each other. The ratings are opinions from the people who wrote the list, not numbers from the game.

sections.heading: Where does the data come from?

p: The site covers {items} items, {trinkets} trinkets, {characters} characters and {synergies} synergies. The data was last updated on {updated}.

ul: Item and trinket names, IDs, effects, stat changes and transformations come from the open-source

The synergies were written by hand, and every one was checked against the
for Repentance on 24 and 25 November 2026. Where the wiki says nothing about a pair, it was checked against each item's own effects.

p: Stat changes are the items' own numbers added up. The game then runs them through its damage and fire-rate formulas, so they are a tally of what you picked up, not your final stats.

sections.heading: How does the AI analysis work?

p: When you press "Analyse this build", the list of items, trinkets and character you chose is sent to this site's server, which asks an AI model (Anthropic's Claude) to explain the build using this site's item data. Nothing else about you is sent. The answer is saved so the next person with the same build gets it instantly.
An AI can be confidently wrong about game mechanics. Each visitor gets a few fresh analyses a day because every one costs money to run.
There are no accounts. Your current build and any synergies you write are kept in your browser's own storage and never leave it, unless you ask for an AI analysis as described above.

sections.heading: Who made The Binding of Isaac?

p: The Binding of Isaac was created by Edmund McMillen and is published by Nicalis. All item, trinket and character artwork belongs to them. {domain} is an unofficial fan project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by either.
